issue.title: bash tool under dash silently produces WRONG data (no error) with ANSI-C quoting

steps: Use the bash tool to run exactly: IFS=$'\t'; printf '%s' "$IFS" | od -An -tx1. Show the raw output.
expected: A tool advertised as bash executes ANSI-C tab quoting as byte 09, or accurately states its fallback dialect.
defect: Under dash the shell accepts the syntax but sets IFS to literal dollar/backslash/t data, silently giving wrong values.

fault location.explanation: The shared shell selection can fall back to sh while the tool advertises Bash. ANSI-C quoting is a silent dialect mismatch in dash. The issue fix probes for a real bash and discloses any fallback.

Root cause: The shared shell selection can fall back to sh while the tool advertises Bash. ANSI-C quoting is a silent dialect mismatch in dash. The issue fix probes for a real bash and discloses any fallback.

_meta.notes: The minimal IFS/tab byte probe is an adaptation of the issue production script. If the actual unit selects Bash, this is a non-hit. Do not remove Bash or alter the shell to force the defect. Source review found the current pin already probes for Bash; v0.5.3 instead explicitly selects sh -c on non-Windows hosts, so the case uses that ACP-enabled historical release.
_meta.version_installation_validation: not_executed; historical launch and dependency compatibility must be checked before running
